test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 29 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I sometimes accept excess work to please my manager, so I __take more responsibilities than one can manage.__

options.text: bite off more than I can chew
get a taste of my own medicine
hear it straight from the horse’s mouth

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**bite off more than I can chew**" means** taking on more responsibility than one can handle, which directly substitutes the underlined segment.**
 
• Other options do not fit the context of taking on too much work.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Explanation:** *The sentence should read, "I sometimes accept excess work to please my manager, so I **bite off more than I can chew**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "get a taste of my own medicine"** – This idiom means to experience the same unpleasant situation that one has caused others, which is not relevant here.
 
• **Option 3: "burn my boats"** – This idiom means to commit to a course of action without being able to turn back, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 4: "hear it straight from the horse's mouth"** – This idiom means to get information directly from the source, which is also irrelevant here.
